subject: Failover liability cap proposal for ClearWave — scope & options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@clearwave.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Failover liability cap proposal for ClearWave — scope & options

Evan —

Thanks again for the thoughtful discussion yesterday. Per follow-up with our delivery and legal teams, I wanted to propose a narrow scope that balances ClearWave's DR needs with the operational constraints of a private Dedicated deployment. High level: we can offer a documented multi-region failover playbook and on-call support for region failovers, but we need to cap contractual obligations around RTO/RPO for automated cross-region failover due to synchronous replication costs and regulatory boundaries.

Key points in the attached "proposed-failover-scope-redwood-v2.pdf":
- Redwood will maintain a warm-standby replica in a secondary EU region; full automated failover is offered as an optional add-on.
- Standard commitment: 99.95% region availability per month for the primary region, with a best-effort coordination for cross-region failover during major outages.
- For guaranteed cross-region automated failover (contractual SLA), we require a premium reserved capacity add-on and an agreed DR runbook with scheduled failover windows; targeted RTO would be 4–10 hours depending on warmup/kv-cache priming.
- If ClearWave needs hard RTO <= 1 hour and RPO <= 1 minute across regions, we must run active-active replication and dedicated networking (higher cost).

We know procurement and security will want clear SLAs. To keep momentum, I'm proposing a middle ground: commit to a 6-hour contractual RTO for documented failovers with a set of remediation credits; provide a timeline and fixed-cost estimate for the <1h RTO upgrade.

Can you review the attached and let me know if ClearWave's legal/procurement would accept a limited-liability clause around cross-region automated failover with the 6-hour RTO baseline? If they push for full multi-region failover guarantees, we'll need to convert to the premium active-active pricing and get sign-off from infra.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.

—Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com
Attachments: proposed-failover-scope-redwood-v2.pdf

From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@clearwave.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@clearwave.io>, Legal Team <legal@clearwave.io>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2027 14:21:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Failover liability cap proposal for ClearWave — scope & options

Naomi —

Appreciate the detailed proposal and the PDF. A few immediate reactions from procurement/legal:

1) ClearWave's platform is customer-facing and regulated across multiple EU countries. Our security team flagged that a 6-hour contractual RTO for cross-region failover is materially higher risk than our policy allows without compensating controls.
2) If Redwood cannot contractually guarantee <= 2-hour RTO for cross-region during critical incidents, we will need to negotiate financial indemnities or credits tied to downtime.
3) Can you provide historical metrics or runbook excerpts that demonstrate how Redwood has executed similar failovers in production? Procurement also requested a short SLA exhibit showing sample credit calculations.

We're open to evaluating the premium active-active option if the pricing makes sense. For next steps, Legal wants a bulletized one-page exhibit we can share internally.

-Evan
Evan Morris
Head of Ops, ClearWave
evam.morris@clearwave.io

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com, priyom_das@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Failover liability cap proposal for ClearWave — scope & options

Marissa / Karthik / Priyom —

Looping you in. ClearWave pushed back hard on 6-hour contractual RTO and asked for <=2 hours or financial indemnity. They also requested historical runbook excerpts and a simple SLA exhibit with credit math. I attached their questionnaire too (clearwave-security-questionnaire-2027.pdf).

Questions:
- Is there a defensible technical argument to keep the contractual RTO at 6 hours for standard Dedicated (non active-active) while offering a defined credit schedule?
- If we offer a 2-hour contractual RTO, what infra changes and cost delta are we looking at (rough order of magnitude)?

Karthik — please advise on technical feasibility/cost for a 2-hour cross-region RTO for a Dedicated pool behind private networking. Priyom — can you sketch a compact SLA exhibit (one page) with sample credit tiers?

Thanks — Naomi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, priyom_das@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Failover liability cap proposal for ClearWave — scope & options

Team —

Short answer: a contractual <=2-hour cross-region RTO for production-grade LLM services at scale requires either (a) active-active with synchronous or near-synchronous replication, or (b) a fully warmed warm-standby with pre-populated KV caches, DNS failover automation, and reserved cross-region bandwidth. Both options have non-trivial cost. Rough numbers:
- Active-active (preferred for <=1h RTO): +40–60% infra cost on top of Dedicated baseline, plus significant networking egress for sync replication.
- Warm-warm standby with 2h RTO: +20–30% infra cost, plus scheduled warmup steps that must be exercised weekly to keep cache primed.

Operational constraints: automated failover under 2 hours also needs runbook gating (DB quiesce, cache rebuild windows) and legal acceptance for planned runbooks. If we keep contractual baseline at 6 hours, we can reduce committed reserved capacity and offer a priced upgrade path to 2h.

I'll attach a short operations appendix for the SLA exhibit (see Drive link) and draft a recommended credit table. We can offer: 6-hour baseline SLA with 0.25% monthly credit per hour beyond RTO up to a cap, or upgrade to 2-hour contractual RTO for a 30% price uplift and a stricter credit schedule.

-Karthik
Director of Infrastructure

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@clearwave.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com, procurement <procurement@clearwave.io>, Legal Team <legal@clearwave.io>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Failover liability cap proposal for ClearWave — scope & options

Evan —

Thanks for the candid feedback. We've pulled together a concise SLA exhibit and an ops appendix (Drive link below) that we think hits the balance:

1) Baseline: 6-hour contractual RTO for cross-region failover for standard Dedicated (documented runbook + monthly warmup exercises). Credit: 0.25% of monthly invoice per hour beyond RTO, capped at 25% of the monthly invoice.
2) Upgrade: 2-hour contractual RTO available as a premium add-on (estimated +30% monthly cost). Credit: 0.5% per hour beyond RTO, capped at 50% of invoice.
3) Active-active: <=1-hour RTO option (requires active-active replication and networking) — pricing provided on request (approx +40–60%).

Attached are the one-page SLA exhibit and a redlined draft clause that limits Redwood's cross-region liability to the defined credit schedule while preserving remediation obligations and an agreed operational cadence for failover drills. If ClearWave's Legal wants stronger indemnities instead of credits, we'll need to escalate pricing and get sign-off from finance.

If this looks reasonable, I'll set up a 45-min review with ClearWave Legal and our finance/legal to finalize the exhibit.

Link to ops appendix & exhibit: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-failover-plan

—Naomi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
